capabilities.name: Authored scene event
capabilities.summary: Run validated dialogue, rewards, flags, challenges and bounded actor choreography on interaction.

configuration.name: repeatable
configuration.limits: Required explicit value; challenge requires true.

configuration.name: note
configuration.limits: Optional 1–320 character discovered journal note; shown only after this event has run.

limits: Choreography supports sequential moves, facing, three reaction cues and waits; no parallel groups or custom animation scripts.
Movement is limited to 128 steps and 4096 inspected cells per destination; waits to 5 seconds.
Scene event history is limited to 256 entries.

examples.intent: Run validated dialogue, rewards, flags, challenges and bounded actor choreography on interaction.
examples.usage: Consult dist/src/domain/scenes.js and reuse the existing definition.
examples.expected: Resolve bounded actor actions and commit durable scene results before transient presentation.

evidence.assertion: Regression coverage of the existing contract; this is not a new visual approval.
Independent evidence alternatives, prerequisite failures, reload and mutually exclusive outcomes.

details.activation: Existing map scene interaction dispatch. Optional landmark.labels conditions disclose the action before interacting; they fall back to the ordinary inspection label and never change map labels.
details.conditions: Optional event/all/any/not and existing objective conditions; map validation rejects unknown scene/route evidence and positive prerequisite cycles. An explicitly configured beforeLandmark prop scene interaction takes precedence over generic landmark text.
details.actions: Dialogue, reward, flag, challenge, move, face, wait and react; challenge must be last. See docs/SCENE_ACTIONS.md for choreography limits.
details.rewards: Scene rewards accept coins, potions and orbs, not arbitrary inventory item IDs.
details.repetition: Explicit repeatable boolean; challenge events must be repeatable.
details.persistence: Non-repeatable events use saved map/event keys; rewards and flags commit before choreography and roll back if saving fails. Optional notes appear in the journal only after the saved event.

capabilities.name: Battle potion
capabilities.summary: Consume the configured battle potion in battle to heal the active companion by its pack-defined effect.
limits: Healing is capped at the companion's maximum HP and requires an available mapped supply.
Does not increase player speed or confer a three-battle buff.

examples.intent: Consume a potion in battle to apply the selected pack's healing effect.
examples.usage: Consult dist/src/domain/battle.js and reuse the existing definition.
examples.expected: Consume one mapped potion and heal the active companion according to its pack definition.

evidence.assertion: Regression coverage of the existing contract; this is not a new visual approval.

details.contexts: Battle action; no claim of an exploration-use interface.
details.consumption: Consumes one available potion on successful use.
details.strength: Pack-defined effect, capped by maximum HP.
details.stacking: Repeated uses heal again up to max HP; no buff stacking.
details.persistence: Remaining supplies and health use the existing battle/save transaction.

capabilities.name: Adventure readiness report
capabilities.summary: Report whether a pack can be built and played, which file and path block it, and what only a person can judge.
limits: It runs the existing validators and the game compiler; it adds no new rules beyond advisory route signals and the repeatable scene reward check.
A 'buildable' result is mechanical only: story meaning, visual composition and enjoyment are always listed as not evaluated, and the browser playthrough is not run.
A one-way entrance is only a warning because the manifest has no field to declare it intentional.
It never writes into the pack or saves; `--out` must point outside the pack folder.

examples.intent: Check a candidate pack before handing it to a reviewer.
examples.usage: Run `npm run adventure:report -- <pack-folder>` (add `--format json` for tools, `--strict` to fail on warnings).
examples.expected: A deterministic Markdown or JSON report with per-check results, errors with file, JSON path and next step, warnings, and the human-review list; exit 0 buildable, 1 blocked, 2 usage, 3 warnings under --strict.

evidence.assertion: A valid pack passes; broken copies (unknown asset, unreachable chest, wrong save schema, missing and malformed files, stale hash, unreachable map, repeatable reward, one-way entrance) fail or warn at the right file and path; output is byte-identical and the pack is never modified; exit codes are stable.

details.trigger: Authoring CLI invocation.
details.inputs: A pack folder containing index.json and the files it selects.
details.sequence: Check files and hashes, manifest, compatibility and registries; compile the adventure with the shared compiler; add advisory route signals and the repeatable-reward check; render sorted JSON or Markdown.
details.results: A report whose status is blocked or buildable, with a separate list of review only a person can do.
details.cancellation: Not applicable; the command is read-only.
details.errors: An unreadable folder or bad option exits 2 without a report; missing or malformed pack files are reported with their path and later dependent checks are skipped.
details.persistence: Nothing is saved or written to the pack; output goes to stdout or an explicit --out file outside the pack.

capabilities.name: Battle impact feedback
capabilities.summary: Show every resolved blow as a floating number, an eased HP bar with a trailing ghost, a held hit flash and a short scene shake, and play orb throws and victories as readable beats, and show your own team changing: recall, send-in, faint and level-up.
limits: Presentation only: it reads the already-resolved turn events and never changes damage, Focus, saves or outcomes.
Calm motion keeps the numbers and final bar widths but drops the shake, sparks and bar easing.
Each round now ends on a settled frame, so the foe's reply stays on screen for 500-700 ms (250 ms in calm motion) before controls return.

Capture beats are derived from the already-resolved throw: a success wobbles three times, a miss wobbles once more the closer it was (1 to 3), and calm motion collapses to a single wobble; the wobble count never changes the outcome.

Victory shows the foe fading, your friend hopping and the XP and coins the rules already granted; it adds about one second before the result screen, and a throw adds about two seconds (shorter in calm motion).

The pre-throw befriended status remains visible during throw/wobble; success is revealed when the orb settles and failure when it opens. Battle actions remain locked until playback ends, including calm motion. The HUD friend count, coin/XP rewards, quest progress and controller notices also wait for the orb result. Durable capture and objective events still commit before playback. Ally level/HP and move information read the pre-throw presentation snapshot until resolution, including a capture that levels up the companion.

Automatic calm motion follows the system media query directly; the CSS override class is reserved for the explicit player setting, so returning to normal system motion cannot leave creature animations stuck.

Team transitions are presentation of already-resolved events: a switch plays recall then send-in, a fainted friend fades before the next steps in (or before the defeat screen), and a level-up gets its own beat; none of them changes who is active, HP, XP or outcomes.
The name line keeps the pre-round level until the level-up beat; calm motion keeps the messages, numbers and order but drops fades, sparks and glows, and each beat is shorter.

examples.intent: Strike a wild creature and read the result at a glance.
examples.usage: Use Quick strike or the Element move; no configuration is needed.
examples.expected: A number floats over the target, the HP bar eases down while a pale ghost lags behind, and a heavier or super-effective hit shakes the scene harder.

examples.intent: Throw a capture orb at a weakened creature.
examples.usage: Press Capture orb (5) or click it; no configuration is needed.
examples.expected: The orb flies in and holds the creature, wobbles, then either settles with a star burst and floating rewards before the result screen, or opens and the creature pops back out.

examples.intent: Switch companions, or lose one in battle.
examples.usage: Choose Switch friend (8), or let a friend fall.
examples.expected: The outgoing friend shrinks away or fades, the next one pops in with sparks, and the log says who came back or stepped in.

evidence.assertion: Events map to floating numbers, tones, shake levels and heals without touching game state.
A real battle shows the strike and the foe's reply as floating numbers, bars ease, and calm motion removes the shake and sparks.

A real throw shows throw, three wobbles and settle with stars and floating rewards; a miss opens the orb and the creature pops out; a win fades the foe and floats XP; calm motion has no sparks and one wobble per throw. Ownership and HUD counters/rewards/quests retain their pre-throw presentation until resolution, including calm motion and repeated captures.
Automatic system reduction disables animation and returns to idle breathing without becoming a sticky manual override.

A switch plays recall then send-in; a fainted friend fades before the replacement steps in or before the defeat result; a level-up beat follows the victory and the name line changes only then; calm motion has no sparks.

details.trigger: A resolved strike, enemy attack, riposte, potion, charge recovery, orb throw or win event. Also a switch, faint, defeat or level-up.
details.inputs: The turn event (damage, effectiveness, action kind, healed amount) and the per-frame HP snapshot.
details.sequence: Each frame draws the bars from the previous frame's width, forces a reflow and sets the new width so the transition runs; numbers rise for 0.9 s; the scene shakes at level 1 or 2. Orb throws expand into throw, wobble and settle-or-open beats; a win adds a victory beat where the foe fades out. Switches expand into recall and send-in beats, a fainted friend into a fade beat (then a send-in or the result), and a level change into a glow beat.
details.results: Damage, healing and effectiveness read without parsing the battle log; numbers are hidden from assistive technology because the log already announces them.
details.cancellation: A new frame replaces the markup; leaving the battle or skipping playback drops pending effects.
details.errors: With no previous width (first frame or a switched companion) the bar is drawn at its final value without easing.
details.persistence: Presentation-only; nothing is saved.

capabilities.name: Local authoring catalogue
capabilities.summary: Generate and validate resource fiches, browse registered art and export selected game visuals or licensed reference sheets for local writers.
limits: Structural and diff checks do not prove prose accuracy; scoped exceptions require reviewer assessment.
Third-party concepts use the separate reference: namespace and are never runtime visuals, species identities or approved Mossvale art.
Reference sheet exports are limited to 2 MiB per image and 16 MiB total per selection; --all exports registered game visuals only.

examples.intent: Give a writer one licensed creature concept sheet to inspect and attach to a design prompt.
examples.usage: Run npm run catalogue:browse, filter by source, subject and license, select the reference: record, copy its ID, then run npm run catalogue:export -- --out=/tmp/writer-context --ids=reference:andhegames/more-assorted-creatures.
examples.expected: A portable index and only the selected image, with creator, source, CC0 terms, hash and limits; the reference has no runtime identity or game behavior.

evidence.assertion: Deterministic generation, source freshness, references and diff-impact failure cases.
Stable reference namespace, source metadata, deterministic selected-image export, hash integrity, symlink rejection and export size bounds.
Reference source/license/subject filters, deferred full-sheet loading and selectable IDs in the local browser.

details.trigger: Run the local visual browser or catalogue export command.
details.inputs: Generated game catalogue and separately curated, hash-checked third-party reference registries.
details.sequence: Filter visuals and references by subject, source or license; load the selected fiche and full sheet on demand; copy selected stable IDs; export only selected images with provenance and limits.
details.results: A portable writer context with catalogue visuals and separate reference: records; reference records are never added to gameplay or save identity.
details.cancellation: No runtime game state changes.
details.errors: Invalid records, unknown IDs, hash mismatches, unsafe or symlinked paths, oversized references and stale catalogue output fail closed.
details.persistence: Checked-in deterministic documentation, not adventure save data.

capabilities.name: Companion route gate
capabilities.summary: Discover and unlock a concealed optional route by approaching it with a compatible companion.
limits: Discovery uses a 2.5-tile approach radius and the active companion's authored ability/habitat tags.
This is not free-form flying, swimming or arbitrary companion interaction.

examples.intent: Discover a secret shortcut with the companion whose abilities fit the route.
examples.usage: Author an exit route in a map, optionally link clue signs with routeHint, then approach within 2.5 tiles while the matching companion is active.
examples.expected: The route, clue sign and map marker appear after discovery; the route event and reward are saved once, and the route remains usable with any companion.

evidence.assertion: Covers hidden/ineligible states, eligible approach, saved discovery/reward, reload and alternate-route recovery.

details.trigger: Move within 2.5 tiles of the authored route with a matching active companion.
details.inputs: Required companion ability/habitat tags, validated route data and optional linked sign routeHint.
details.sequence: Keep the route, linked hints and map marker concealed until eligible approach; save its stable event and grant the reward once.
details.results: The optional route and linked hint become visible and remain traversable by every companion without removing the alternate path.
details.cancellation: Ineligible companion keeps the normal boardwalk available.
details.errors: Unknown route references fail map validation.
details.persistence: Unlock/reward use saved scene event keys; legacy exploration markers alone do not reveal the route.

capabilities.name: Complete creature frame extraction

configuration.name: creature-combat-v1

configuration.name: --species / --strict-source-grid / --check / --preview-dir
configuration.limits: Select a species, reject crowded new sources, verify without mutation and inspect raw/segmented/anchored/runtime stages. All selected inputs preflight before writes.

limits: Legacy recovery preserves original foreground pixels before fitting; it cannot invent missing anatomy or repair a different creature design.
Indexed species keep their existing no-dither palette conversion.
The spacing audit verifies hashes, clear margins and baselines; visual review at gameplay scale remains separate from owner taste.

examples.intent: Review a newly generated Emberkin combat sheet without replacing runtime art.
examples.usage: python3 art/characters/export-creature-combat.py --root /tmp/creature-candidate --species emberkin --strict-source-grid --check --preview-dir /tmp/creature-review
examples.expected: Reject crowded or missing cells, inspect all four stages and leave runtime files unchanged.

evidence.assertion: Nonuniform rows, thin tails, detached particles, alpha holes, pixel conservation, shared scale, transparent gutters and 360 combat frames.
Exact runtime hashes and margin/baseline audit for 40 atlases and 1,160 cells.
Recorded complete-pose review at 115 px, pinned to current outputs and contact sheet; owner taste remains pending.

details.trigger: Authoring or verifying a creature combat source sheet.
details.inputs: Generated RGBA source, canonical reference, category profile and reviewed legacy separation settings.
details.sequence: Preflight selected sources, identify body ownership, restore original foreground, fit once per species, anchor and compare/write staged outputs.
details.results: Complete 4x5 combat atlas with transparent margins, unchanged state IDs and common baseline.
details.cancellation: --check never writes outputs; invalid input stops before staging.
details.errors: Missing bodies, invalid boundaries, inadequate new-source gutters or output mismatch fail with diagnostics.
details.persistence: Changes source/output provenance and authoring evidence only; no game save or combat rule changes.

Reuses optional five-state creature combat atlases or static portraits. Normal action duration, damage, saves, RNG and rewards are unchanged.
Calm motion shows one static material-specific impact without travel or camera shake. Internal art review does not imply owner taste approval.

examples.intent: Use a Fire companion elemental move in an encounter.

examples.expected: A branching lightning bolt connects enemy to ally in the mirrored direction; ally HP updates at contact.

evidence.assertion: Exercises all twelve elements in actual battles on both sides with normal/reduced motion, contact timing, legacy fallback, landscape bounds and cancellation.
Covers canonical element mapping, unchanged beat durations, pre-contact HP/audio, mirroring and clamped geometry.

details.inputs: Canonical species type display-name, resolved event, pre-hit snapshot, optional six-pose effect atlas and existing creature attack pose.
details.sequence: Normal 650 ms ally or 700 ms enemy beat: prepare, directed travel, contact/dissolve. Reveal HP, damage text, pops, target recoil and audio only at contact. Calm motion uses one 250 ms static impact.
details.results: Leaf blades, water splash, rock, fireball, ice spears, lightning, wind, spores, petals, mud, sand and frost use distinct authored silhouettes/materials.

capabilities.name: Guardian counterplay rewards
capabilities.summary: Show the next guardian action and matchup-based damage, then reward a valid tactical response when the fight is won.
limits: Damage is a random-roll range for the current active companion; switching changes the matchup and forecast.

Bonuses are granted once per qualifying response in one guardian fight; they do not make any single creature mandatory. A response that requires a later enemy action is not credited if the guardian is defeated first.

examples.intent: Read a guardian's next action, compare current and Guard damage, and choose a response before its turn.
examples.usage: Configure counterplay in a tactic under dist/maps/registries.json and use the existing Guard action.
examples.expected: The forecast identifies action order, damage ranges, current Focus or response availability; a qualifying response is named with bonus coins and XP on victory.

evidence.assertion: Damage-range parity with the resolver; brace, repeated-element, charge and heavy timing; response qualification, payout, checkpoint persistence and invalid-ID filtering.
Forecast remains legible in keyboard, touch, reduced-motion and fullscreen browser states.

details.trigger: While a guardian battle is idle, the interface previews its next tactic action and any relevant response window.
details.inputs: The deterministic tactic pattern position, species damage formula, current active matchup, Guard factor, Focus, party health and configured response conditions.
details.sequence: Derive the upcoming action, unguarded and guarded random damage ranges, brace or charge effects and matching responses without mutating battle state. The existing resolver independently records only qualifying player actions and pays recorded bonuses on victory.
details.results: The battle panel explains whether the guardian acts after the player's choice, the current ally's damage range, Guard reduction/riposte, Focus cost, next brace/charge consequence, and any available response reward.
details.cancellation: The forecast is hidden while an action resolves or the battle ends. A lost or abandoned fight pays no response bonus; a saved interrupted fight retains recorded responses. A response requiring the guardian's next action is not recorded if the player's action defeats it first.
details.errors: Unknown response IDs in a saved battle are discarded during normalization.
details.persistence: The forecast is derived and adds no save fields. Recorded response IDs remain part of the existing battle checkpoint and compatible with older saves.

capabilities.name: Pack and save compatibility contract
capabilities.summary: State which engine, save-schema and pack-format levels a pack may declare, and explain a rejection before any save is touched.
limits: The support window is one level wide today (engine 1, save schema 5, pack format 1), so a pack must declare exactly those levels; a wider window ships only together with a tested save migration.
Declared levels are metadata outside the integrity hashes; they are as honest as the tool that stamped them.
No migration registry exists yet because there has been no real schema change since schema 5.
It judges the manifest only; whether a pack's content still plays well after an engine update needs the adventure readiness report and a playtest.

examples.intent: Find out why a pack built for another game level is refused.
examples.usage: Run `npm run adventure:report -- <pack-folder>` or `npm run pack -- validate-pack <pack-folder>`.
examples.expected: The compatibility result names `requires.engineVersion` or `requires.saveSchema` and says whether to update the game or port the pack; the game itself shows the same message at startup before reading any save.

evidence.assertion: The shipped and fixture manifests are compatible; levels above, below and inside a widened window are classified distinctly; missing, string, fractional and non-positive levels are invalid; the loader rejects each case after fetching only index.json; a future save stays untouched and unwritable.

details.trigger: Loading a pack in the game, or running validate-pack, the readiness report or a build.
details.inputs: The pack manifest's format and requires levels and the installed support window.
details.sequence: Fetch index.json, judge each level, stop with a specific message on any problem, then verify file hashes and only then open the save codec.
details.results: compatible, requires-newer-game, pack-too-old or invalid, with the field that caused it.
details.cancellation: Not applicable.
details.errors: A rejected pack shows a retryable startup error naming the field and whether to update the game or port the pack.
details.persistence: Nothing is written; no save, checkpoint, archive or quarantine entry is created or replaced by a rejection.

limits: Geometry and reviewed evidence do not establish owner taste or enjoyment.

Real keyboard/touch controls, actual sprite/UI bounds and once-only rewards on desktop and phone.

details.inputs: Scene intent, selected catalogue resources, runtime pack, hashed captures and separate visual/narrative review.
details.sequence: Validate brief; drive real controls; capture renderer/layout; inspect screenshots and narrative purpose; generate revision-bound report.
details.results: Explicit four-category report, readiness for owner testing and separate owner approval status.
details.cancellation: Required gaps, missing/stale evidence, obscured actors/text/controls or incomplete review prevent readiness.
details.errors: Strict new-scene mode rejects missing payoff/brief; legacy validation emits incomplete-quality warnings. Unsafe/missing evidence paths fail closed.
details.persistence: Authoring artifacts only; canonical pack/save behavior and archived proofs are unchanged.

capabilities.name: Regional route atlas
capabilities.summary: A spoiler-safe route graph of the adventure on the map screen: visited, known and locked places and the trails between them.
limits: Derived entirely from validated exits and the save's existing discovery records; a pack needs no extra data, but a place with no exit chain to a shown place is parked on its own row.
Places and concealed routes appear only after a visit, a noticed trail sign or a discovered route; hidden places are never named or counted.

Selecting a place only shows facts. Travel is offered only for visited places in an open region and uses the existing travel action; it never makes a merely known place reachable or changes progression.
Layout is a coarse grid from the side each exit leaves its map; it is not a scaled geographic map, and trails that need a different side to avoid overlap may be nudged.

examples.intent: See how the places you have found connect.
examples.usage: Press M, then choose Atlas.
examples.expected: Your current place, visited places and noticed destinations appear as a graph; locked trails are dashed and name the seal that opens them; a text route list repeats it.

evidence.assertion: Fresh, partial and completed saves disclose exactly the right places; a completed atlas has one edge per connected exit pair; concealed routes stay hidden until discovered; layout is deterministic and non-overlapping.

Through real play a noticed sign adds a known place without travel, the disclosure survives reload, visited places offer travel, arrow keys and Enter work, a concealed route appears only once discovered, the phone layout fits, and the Island cards still offer travel.

details.trigger: Opening the map screen and choosing Atlas.
details.inputs: Compiled maps (exits), visitedMaps, noticed trail signs (explored.seen), discovered route events, seal flags and region unlock state.
details.sequence: Compute disclosure, lay out places from exit directions, draw an SVG graph, a detail panel and a text route list; selection follows focus and clicks.
details.results: A readable, keyboard-operable route picture that never exposes a secret route, map label, creature or landmark before its discovery rule.
details.cancellation: Closing the map discards the view; nothing is stored.
details.errors: A save that lists unknown maps or no visited map shows just the current place.
details.persistence: Read-only; it adds nothing to the save.

capabilities.name: Responsive playfield and readable name tags
capabilities.summary: On desktop the game frame fits the window height and renders more of the world in wider windows; character and landmark name tags are drawn on top, outlined and kept apart.
limits: Desktop layout only (width 1000 px or more, height 540 px or more); phones and small windows keep the existing 3:2 frame at 960 px of world width.
World width is capped at 1800 canvas pixels; the Zoom setting still magnifies the world.
Name tags that cannot be placed without overlapping after four upward nudges are skipped for that frame; the objects stay interactable.
Presentation only: movement, collision, encounters, saves and the camera follow rule are unchanged.

examples.intent: Play on a 1080p monitor.
examples.usage: Open the game in a maximised window; no setting is needed.
examples.expected: The whole frame, controls included, fits without scrolling and shows noticeably more of the surrounding map than at 1280x720.

evidence.assertion: At 1280x720, 1366x768, 1920x1080 and 2560x1440 the frame fits the window, the canvas keeps the on-screen aspect and wider windows render at least as much world; phones keep 960 px.

details.trigger: Window resize, fullscreen change or first load.
details.inputs: The canvas bounding box and the 960/1800 pixel width limits.
details.sequence: resize() sets the canvas width to one pixel per CSS pixel above 960 and derives the height from the box; the renderer already reads canvas.width and canvas.height every frame, so visible tiles and objects follow. Labels are collected during the object pass and drawn afterwards, farthest first.
details.results: More world on large screens, no vertical scrolling to reach controls, and name tags that stay legible over foliage.
details.cancellation: Not applicable.
details.errors: A zero-size box (hidden tab) leaves the previous canvas size untouched.
details.persistence: Nothing is saved; the Zoom setting keeps its existing storage.
